newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil Cardoso reaffirms CVRD selloff in '97 - paper.
newsitem.headline: Brazil Cardoso reaffirms CVRD selloff in '97 - paper.

text.p: Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso reaffirmed the sell-off of state mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) in 1997, saying opposition in the Senate posed no threat, a newspaper said.

Cardoso dismissed the importance of the opposition mounted by former Brazilian presidents Itamar Franco and Jose Sarney and former vice-president Aureliano Chaves, saying they were a minority in the Senate which still has to authorize the sell-off, Gazeta Mercantil said.
"There is always a group which opposes, there always has been and always will be," Cardoso was quoted as saying by Gazeta. "It's a sector which has its arguments, but it's a minority in the Senate."

Cardoso, who was speaking at the Ibero-American summit in Vina del Mar in Chile, said "the whole matter was resolved in the Senate" and there had been "many talks on how the privatization would proceed", Gazeta said.
He added the privatization process would ensure that CVRD would be preserved in its integrity as a mining, ports and railway operation.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
